Add data to a plan

Source: R/plan.R
add_data.Rd

add_data() adds the data name to the plnr plan p, as the steps raw, clean, cohort and after_cohort, or as one data function fn. plnr calls it once for each scenario and simulation, and gives the data to each analysis of that scenario and simulation.

Usage

add_data(
  p,
  name,
  fn = NULL,
  raw = NULL,
  clean = NULL,
  cohort = NULL,
  after_cohort = NULL,
  cache = FALSE
)

Arguments

p

A plan from plnr::Plan$new().

name

The name of the data. Each action function gets it as data[[name]].

fn

The free form: one data function, for data that does not fit the steps. Give fn or raw, not both.

raw

The first step, normally data_raw, a function(scenario, sim) that reads the real data or makes fake data.

clean

Optional. The step that gets the value of raw, normally data_clean, for example for names and types. It MUST return a data.frame with the same number of rows.

cohort

Optional. The step that gets the value of clean, or of raw without clean, normally data_cohort. It MUST return a cohort::CohortPipeline that starts with every row that it got.

after_cohort

Optional, and only with cohort. The step that gets the cohort::CohortPipeline, for example an imputation. It returns the data for the analyses, and pbn puts the exclusion table of the cohort on it. See the section A cohort as the data.

cache

TRUE saves the data on disk for each scenario and simulation. The next run reads it while the cache key is the same. See the section Cache.

Value

Invisibly, the name of the data.

Details

In the steps form, each rule for fn in this section and in the section Cache applies to raw.

plnr keys a data function on its arguments without a default. These are the key fields. Each key field of fn MUST be scenario, sim or a setting column of CFG$scenarios. Otherwise run_plan() stops before it runs anything. plnr calls fn once for each set of values of the key fields, and gives each analysis with those values the same data.

add_data() stops on these arguments of fn:

  • scenario or sim with a default. plnr does not key on it, so every scenario or simulation would get the same data.

  • sim without scenario. Every scenario would get the same data.

A data function without scenario and sim, for example one that reads a lookup table, runs once for the whole run and sets no seed.

pbn adds fn in a wrapper. The wrapper has the key fields of fn as its arguments, so plnr keys it in the same way. It calls fn with them by name, so another argument of fn with a default keeps its default. When sim is an argument, the wrapper calls set.seed(sim) before fn. The data of simulation k is thus the same in each run, and does not depend on the other scenarios of the run. A function that is called with no sim sets no seed.

The wrapper needs no object of the R session that adds it. run_plan() gives each worker the objects that the functions folder defines.

name MUST be one syntactic name that starts with a letter and holds only letters, digits, . and _, for example "d". pbn names each step of the data <name>$<step> in the code that fake_md5 hashes. A $ in a name could thus match a step of another data. name MUST NOT be "hash", because plnr adds data$hash to the data of each analysis. Two data functions of one plan MUST NOT have the same name. Add data with add_data(), not with p$add_data(). save_results() reads the data functions of add_data() only.

While run_plan() runs, an error in fn or in a step fails each analysis that gets the data. When you call get_data() or p$get_data() by hand, the error stops the call.

The steps

pbn runs the steps in the order raw, clean, cohort and after_cohort, and gives the value of each step to the next one. Each step after raw MUST take exactly one argument without a default, or add_data() stops. pbn calls set.seed(sim) once, before raw. So raw = data_raw, clean = data_clean draws the same numbers as fn = function(scenario, sim) data_clean(data_raw(scenario, sim)).

pbn sees the value between the steps, so it checks the rule that the cleaning drops no row. Each exclusion goes through the cohort, which counts it. These values fail the data, as an error in fn does:

  • raw returns a data.frame, and clean returns a value that is not a data.frame, or a data.frame with another number of rows.

  • cohort returns a value that is not a cohort::CohortPipeline.

  • cohort gets a data.frame, and its pipeline starts with another number of rows, cp$n_total().

The error gives both numbers of rows. The checks compare the numbers of rows only, so the order of the rows and the columns MAY change. The checks compare the number of rows, not which rows: a step that drops one row and repeats another passes.

When raw returns a value that is not a data.frame, pbn does not check clean. An example is a list of two tables that clean joins. That list has no number of rows to compare, and it is a valid start. pbn does not check the rows of after_cohort.

Use fn for data that does not fit the steps, for example data that joins two cohorts. pbn then checks no rows inside fn.

An exclusion MAY apply to the rows of a reshape, for example one row for each person and time point. Add these rows as a second data element, with a second call of add_data(). Its raw builds the reshaped rows, and its cohort applies the exclusion, so the cohort counts it. Its raw MAY reshape the value of the raw of the first element. pbn sets the seed to sim before each data element, so both draw the same numbers.

A cohort as the data

fn or the step cohort MAY return a cohort::CohortPipeline after its exclusions. The analyses then get data[[name]] as the data.table of $get_included(<cohort>). <cohort> is the one cohort of the pipeline that no other cohort branches from. A pipeline with more than one such cohort fails the data. Each other value goes to the analyses as it is.

The step after_cohort reads the data of the cohort with cohort_data(), and returns its value. The value MAY be any R object other than NULL, for example a list of imputed data sets. pbn puts the exclusion table of the cohort and its number of rows at the start on the value, as keep_exclusions() does. These replace the attributes that the step set. So a call of keep_exclusions() in the step changes nothing, and a table from another cohort does not stay. The step MAY return the cohort::CohortPipeline that it got. Another cohort::CohortPipeline fails the data, because its exclusion table would replace that of the step cohort.

A step after the cohort in fn returns its value through keep_exclusions(), which puts the exclusion table on it.

pbn keeps the exclusion table of the cohort, and save_results() stores it in the element exclusions of the results. The table has one row for each exclusion step of the cohort and of the cohorts above it, in the order of the exclusion steps. It is a data.frame with these columns:

  • data, the name of the data.

  • step, the reason of $exclude_and_track().

  • n_before, n_excluded and n_after, the number of rows before the step, excluded by the step, and after the step. n_excluded and n_after are n_excluded and n_remaining of $consort().

The value carries the table in its attribute pbn_exclusions, and the number of rows given to the pipeline in its attribute pbn_n_before. save_results() writes that number to manifest$n_rows_before_exclusions. The attributes are how both come back from a worker: the R6 object stays on the worker.

Cache

With cache = TRUE, fn MUST have the arguments scenario and sim without a default. Call initialize_project() first. For each scenario and simulation, run_plan() writes the value to <home>/<version>_cache_gitexclude/<name>/<scenario>/sim_<kkkk>.qs2. The value is the data.table and its exclusion table for a cohort. The cache key goes to sim_<kkkk>_key.qs2 in the same folder. The cache key is the md5 of these parts:

  • the scenario, the simulation and the settings of the scenario.

  • for "real" only, the fingerprint of the data at the time of the use. It holds the name <folder name>/<path in the folder>, the size and the modification time of each file under each folder of folders of initialize_project(). pbn reads no content of a data file. The path of a folder is not in the key. So the same files in another place give the same key when they keep their modification times. A copy with new times looks like changed data, so the data is computed again. A file that changed in place, and kept its size and its modification time, is not seen.

  • the md5 of each file of <version>_functions/ whose name starts with data_, for example data_raw.R, data_clean.R, data_cohort.R and data_impute.R. initialize_project() computes them before it sources the files.

  • the code of fn, or of each step, deparsed without its source references.

  • CFG$data, when CFG has the element data. Put the config that the data code reads there. A change in another element of CFG does not change the key.

  • the versions of R and pbn. The version of R covers the base packages.

  • the three parts of RNGkind().

The key file also records the version of each package that was loaded in the R session that computed the value, after fn returned. On a worker, that is the worker. The record leaves out the base packages. It also leaves out the packages that run the plan, tests and documents: pbn, plnr, foreach, doParallel, doFuture, future, future.apply, globals, listenv, parallelly, progressr, iterators, qs2, digest, uuid, progress, testthat, pkgload, devtools, callr, processx, ps, knitr, rmarkdown and evaluate. A later use compares each recorded version with utils::packageVersion() now. A package with another version, or one that is not installed now, computes the value again.

Each use of the cache stops when a data_*.R file on disk differs from the file that initialize_project() hashed and sourced: changed, added or removed. The error names the file. Run initialize_project() again. A file with its recorded size and modification time is not hashed again, so a change that keeps both is not found.

Keep the data code in the files data_*.R. The key holds no other file. A function of the data code can be in another file. A change in it then leaves the key the same, and the run reads the old data. This is the one change of the data code that the cache does not find.

When the key is the same, run_plan() reads the value from the cache and does not call fn or a step. Each analysis sets its own seed, so its results are the same as with a new value. Otherwise, or when a cache file cannot be read, it calls fn or the steps and writes the cache. To compute every value again, delete the folder <version>_cache_gitexclude/. No argument does that.

For each scenario and simulation, run_plan() prints one line with cat(). The line says that the data came from the cache, with the date and time of the cache file. Or it says that pbn computed it, and why. The reason names each changed data_*.R file, CFG$data, or the settings. It names changed raw data with its folders, for example "the raw data in the folder lookup". It names a changed fn as "the data function of add_data()", and each changed step as, for example, "the function given as clean". It can also name the kind of random number generator, or each package with another version. With workers = 1, the line comes before the data function runs. With more workers, run_plan() prints the lines after the run, in the order of the plan.

run_plan() writes each file to a temporary file in the same folder, and renames it. plnr runs the data of one scenario and simulation in one task, so two workers of one run never write the same file. When two runs write one file at the same time, the last rename wins, and each file is whole. The cache file holds its key too, so a cache file and a key file from two runs give a new computation.

The cache folder holds data for each person. When the project is a git repository, git MUST ignore it: run_plan() stops before it runs anything when git does not ignore the cache files. Add the line *gitexclude* to the .gitignore of the project.

p$get_data() and p$run_one() by hand use the cache too, and print the same line. pbn computes the key at the time of the call, with the same rules.

See also

vignette("pbn"), which builds and runs a small fake project.

Other plan: add_analyses(), cohort_data(), get_data(), progress(), run_plan()

Examples

p <- plnr::Plan$new()
pbn::add_data(
  p,
  "d",
  raw = function(scenario, sim) return(data.frame(X = stats::rnorm(3))),
  clean = function(d) return(stats::setNames(d, tolower(names(d))))
)
